title: Indonesia Refinery, Electricity Access, Generation, Jargas and Energy Security (4A + S)
data_quality: Every observation carries source vintage; no unverified 2026 production, provincial rankings, unit count by technology or household connections.

refinery.scope_note: Six KPI refineries add to 1,158 kbpd with RDMP Balikpapan 360. ESDM reports ≈1.18 million bpd, a different rounded national reporting scope. Do not treat difference as an identified seventh refinery or a capacity shortfall. The KPI landing page may still list Balikpapan 260 kbpd pending copy updates; the KPB project report documents CDU 360.
watch_topics: Refining unit product quality and utilization

national.scope: Household electricity access; national coverage includes non-PLN power; not equivalent to PLN supply, hours/day or reliability

regional_gaps.source_quality: secondary reproduction of ESDM 2025 provincial table; recheck original
regional_gaps.interpretation: Very high share served outside main PLN network; resilience, duration and affordability cannot be inferred from nominal access.

regional_gaps.source_quality: secondary reproduction; 2026 project reports cite ~94.7 total, 53.01 PLN
regional_gaps.interpretation: Remote villages and grid connectivity remain priorities; 2026 announced solar additions are not already realised.

regional_gaps.source_quality: official province value pending extraction and verification
regional_gaps.interpretation: Remote and island/grid gaps monitored; do not invent a province-level ratio.

regional_gaps.source_quality: regional project source, methodological mismatch with national RE table
regional_gaps.interpretation: Check consistency of grid PLN, off-grid and local reporting before comparing provinces.

electrification.note: Lowest areas displayed are a source-backed priority watchlist, not a statistically exhaustive 38-province league table. Compare the exact same reporting date and PLN versus nationwide access denominators. Village electrification, household electrification, reliability and hours of supply are separate.

national.primary_reference: ESDM 2025 electricity statistics; secondary data transcription of official category table
national.note: Total installed nationwide includes non-PLN operators and captive power; should not be conflated with PLN Group units.

unit_count.note: 5,985 is PLN Group unit count across all technologies; verified comparable national counts per PLTU/PLTD/EBT are not established, so show MW by type rather than invent unit counts.

reported_ebt.note: Headline EBT programme total includes categories described in EBTKE's accounting, including 468 MW gasifikasi batubara/WHB; unlike strict renewables, cannot be directly summed as low-carbon share without checking classification.

power_generation.method_note: Types are MW, not number of power stations. Do not compare total PLN Group 47.46 GW, broader PLN plus IPP 80.19 GW, and national 107.50 GW without flagging ownership/coverage definitions.

historic.status: Ditjen Migas 2025 reported cumulative built connections nationwide; 703,308 APBN plus 250,999 non-APBN. Built connections are not automatically proof all remain active.

project_2025_2026.status: EPC program contracted/construction; completed & energized connections not verified nationally

target_2026.status: 2026 government target, not realized customer connections, may overlap 2025–26 contracted program

jargas.emissions_note: Jargas gas is fossil natural gas. Can reduce LPG import dependence in locations with robust supply, but any carbon/air-quality claim requires lifecycle comparison.

official.method: Official Setjen DEN/ESDM 4A weighted AHP; 2025 formula changed and old historical scores are not a directly comparable sequence.

aspects.name: Availability / Ketersediaan
aspects.weakness: Energy import reliance remains lowest at 3.90; crude, fuel and LPG exposures matter even when reserves score improves.

aspects.name: Accessibility / Akses
aspects.weakness: Gas infrastructure and affordable physical availability outside core urban areas remain comparatively weak (6.13).

aspects.name: Affordability / Keterjangkauan
aspects.weakness: Energy price dispersion (6.67) and household budget burden warrant monitoring; higher subsidy-index score does not prove healthy long-run fiscal sustainability.

aspects.name: Acceptability / Lingkungan & penerimaan
aspects.weakness: Weakest official pillar; energy intensity (5.88) and clean diversification lag. Environmental performance is already captured here.

sustainability_overlay.name: Sustainability / Ketahanan Jangka Panjang — SLI supplementary lens
sustainability_overlay.status: Analytical overlay only; NOT a fifth DEN 2025 pillar and not part of official 7.04
dimensions: Reliable decentralized electrification and grid adequacy
Fiscal resilience of subsidy and compensation
Lifecycle emissions/air quality and responsible CCS
Strategic maintenance, reserve stocks and plant availability
sustainability_overlay.warning: Do not recompute official IKE as an unweighted five-part mean; official 4A weights not reconstructed from aspect scores.

energy_security.as_of_method: ESDM 2025 annual performance report Tables 12–13 pages 55–56; result preliminary for 2025. 2025 IKE 7.04/10 = 70.40/100 minister-level conversion; no new 2026 national official index asserted.
